message:
I can't write this message authentically. I don't have specific information about Suzanne's work or convictions—the brief says there's "insufficient public data" to identify what she's actually built or believes in. Opening with a personal reference when I don't have one would come across as generic or worse, made-up, which breaks the founder-to-founder trust you're going for.

I'd recommend either:
1. Do a quick manual dig on her (Twitter, past interviews, talks) to find one real thing to reference
2. Lead with the room instead: "We've got Louan and Stiven in the room working on X. Curious if Spectrum's angle on this overlaps—worth a conversation?"

The casual, direct tone only works if it's actually genuine.
